## Integrability Conditions for the System
$$A\,dx+B\,dy+C\,dz+D\,dt=0,\qquad E\,dx+F\,dy+G\,dz+H\,dt=0.$$

### 1. Setup

Introduce the two 1-forms on the 4‑manifold with coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$:
$$\omega_1=A\,dx+B\,dy+C\,dz+D\,dt,\qquad \omega_2=E\,dx+F\,dy+G\,dz+H\,dt,$$
where $A,\dots,H$ are smooth functions of $(x,y,z,t)$. Write the coefficient vectors
$$a=(A,B,C,D),\qquad e=(E,F,G,H),\qquad x=(x,y,z,t)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4).$$

### 2. Frobenius criterion

The Pfaffian system $\{\omega_1=0,\;\omega_2=0\}$ is **completely integrable** (i.e. admits a 2‑parameter family of integral surfaces) if and only if the differential ideal it generates is closed under exterior differentiation:
$$\boxed{d\omega_1\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0,\qquad d\omega_2\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0.}$$
Each left–hand side is a 4‑form on a 4‑manifold, hence a scalar multiple of $dx\wedge dy\wedge dz\wedge dt$; integrability is the vanishing of those two scalars.

### 3. Computing the scalar

Let $\Omega=\omega_1\wedge\omega_2$ with components $\Omega_{ij}=a_i e_j-a_j e_i$ ($i<j$):
$$\Omega_{xy}=AF-BE,\;\Omega_{xz}=AG-CE,\;\Omega_{xt}=AH-DE,\;\Omega_{yz}=BG-CF,\;\Omega_{yt}=BH-DF,\;\Omega_{zt}=CH-DG.$$

For any 1‑form $\omega=p\cdot dx$ one has $d\omega\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=\langle d\omega,\,*\Omega\rangle\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz\wedge dt$, so the relevant scalar is
$$R(p)=\sum_{i<j}(\partial_i p_j-\partial_j p_i)\,(*\Omega)_{ij},$$
i.e. the Hodge inner product of the curl of $p$ with $\Omega$. Expanding the six independent pairings of $\{x,y,z,t\}$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
R(p)=\;&(CH-DG)(\partial_x p_y-\partial_y p_x)+(AF-BE)(\partial_z p_t-\partial_t p_z)\\
&-(BH-DF)(\partial_x p_z-\partial_z p_x)-(AG-CE)(\partial_y p_t-\partial_t p_y)\\
&+(BG-CF)(\partial_x p_t-\partial_t p_x)+(AH-DE)(\partial_y p_z-\partial_z p_y).
\end{aligned}
$$

### 4. The two integrability conditions

Setting $p=a$ (for $d\omega_1$) and $p=e$ (for $d\omega_2$), and using subscript notation $A_y\equiv\partial A/\partial y$ etc., the integrability conditions $R(a)=0$ and $R(e)=0$ read explicitly:

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(A_y-B_x\bigr)(CH-DG)+\bigl(C_t-D_z\bigr)(AF-BE)\\
&-\bigl(A_z-C_x\bigr)(BH-DF)-\bigl(B_t-D_y\bigr)(AG-CE)\\
&+\bigl(A_t-D_x\bigr)(BG-CF)+\bigl(B_z-C_y\bigr)(AH-DE)=0,
\end{aligned}}
$$

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(E_y-F_x\bigr)(CH-DG)+\bigl(G_t-H_z\bigr)(AF-BE)\\
&-\bigl(E_z-G_x\bigr)(BH-DF)-\bigl(F_t-H_y\bigr)(AG-CE)\\
&+\bigl(E_t-H_x\bigr)(BG-CF)+\bigl(F_z-G_y\bigr)(AH-DE)=0.
\end{aligned}}
$$

### 5. Verification of the structure

* **Consistency check (integrable case).** Take $\omega_1=dx,\;\omega_2=dy$, i.e. $A=F=1$ and all other coefficients zero. Every curl vanishes, so both left–hand sides are $0$; the system $dx=0,dy=0$ is indeed integrable (integral surfaces $x=\text{const},y=\text{const}$). ✓
* **Non‑trivial integrable case.** Take $\omega_1=dx,\;\omega_2=x\,dy$: $d\omega_1=0$ and $d\omega_2=dx\wedge dy$, so $d\omega_2\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=dx\wedge dy\wedge dx\wedge(x\,dy)=0$. In the formula, $R(a)=0$ (constants) and $R(e)$ has only $E_y-F_x=0-1=-1$ multiplying $CH-DG=0$, while every other factor carries a vanishing $\Omega$‑coefficient; hence $R(e)=0$. ✓
* **Symmetry.** The second condition is obtained from the first by the simultaneous replacement $A\to E,\;B\to F,\;C\to G,\;D\to H$ *in the curl factors only*; the bilinear $\Omega$‑factors $(CH-DG),(AF-BE),\dots$ are common to both, exactly as expected since both conditions test closure of the *same* ideal generated by $\omega_1,\omega_2$.

### 6. Equivalent compact form

Using the Levi‑Civita symbol $\varepsilon_{ijmn}$ (indices in $\{x,y,z,t\}$), both conditions unify into the single statement
$$\varepsilon_{ijmn}\,a_m\,e_n\,\partial_i p_j=0,\qquad p\in\{a,e\},$$
i.e. $\langle d\omega_p,\,\*(\omega_1\wedge\omega_2)\rangle=0$ for $p=1,2$. This is precisely $d\omega_p\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0$, confirming the two boxed scalar equations above are the explicit Frobenius integrability conditions for the given system.

## Integrability Conditions for the System
$$A\,dx+B\,dy+C\,dz+D\,dt=0,\qquad E\,dx+F\,dy+G\,dz+H\,dt=0.$$

### 1. Setup

Introduce the two 1-forms on the 4‑manifold with coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$:
$$\omega_1=A\,dx+B\,dy+C\,dz+D\,dt,\qquad \omega_2=E\,dx+F\,dy+G\,dz+H\,dt,$$
where $A,\dots,H$ are smooth functions of $(x,y,z,t)$. Write the coefficient vectors
$$a=(A,B,C,D),\qquad e=(E,F,G,H),\qquad x=(x,y,z,t)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4).$$

### 2. Frobenius criterion

The Pfaffian system $\{\omega_1=0,\;\omega_2=0\}$ is **completely integrable** (i.e. admits a 2‑parameter family of integral surfaces) if and only if the differential ideal it generates is closed under exterior differentiation:
$$\boxed{d\omega_1\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0,\qquad d\omega_2\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0.}$$
Each left–hand side is a 4‑form on a 4‑manifold, hence a scalar multiple of $dx\wedge dy\wedge dz\wedge dt$; integrability is the vanishing of those two scalars.

### 3. Computing the scalar

Let $\Omega=\omega_1\wedge\omega_2$ with components $\Omega_{ij}=a_i e_j-a_j e_i$ ($i<j$):
$$\Omega_{xy}=AF-BE,\;\Omega_{xz}=AG-CE,\;\Omega_{xt}=AH-DE,\;\Omega_{yz}=BG-CF,\;\Omega_{yt}=BH-DF,\;\Omega_{zt}=CH-DG.$$

For any 1‑form $\omega=p\cdot dx$ one has $d\omega\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=\langle d\omega,\,*\Omega\rangle\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz\wedge dt$, so the relevant scalar is
$$R(p)=\sum_{i<j}(\partial_i p_j-\partial_j p_i)\,(*\Omega)_{ij},$$
i.e. the Hodge inner product of the curl of $p$ with $\Omega$. Expanding the six independent pairings of $\{x,y,z,t\}$ gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
R(p)=\;&(CH-DG)(\partial_x p_y-\partial_y p_x)+(AF-BE)(\partial_z p_t-\partial_t p_z)\\
&-(BH-DF)(\partial_x p_z-\partial_z p_x)-(AG-CE)(\partial_y p_t-\partial_t p_y)\\
&+(BG-CF)(\partial_x p_t-\partial_t p_x)+(AH-DE)(\partial_y p_z-\partial_z p_y).
\end{aligned}
$$

### 4. The two integrability conditions

Setting $p=a$ (for $d\omega_1$) and $p=e$ (for $d\omega_2$), and using subscript notation $A_y\equiv\partial A/\partial y$ etc., the integrability conditions $R(a)=0$ and $R(e)=0$ read explicitly:

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(A_y-B_x\bigr)(CH-DG)+\bigl(C_t-D_z\bigr)(AF-BE)\\
&-\bigl(A_z-C_x\bigr)(BH-DF)-\bigl(B_t-D_y\bigr)(AG-CE)\\
&+\bigl(A_t-D_x\bigr)(BG-CF)+\bigl(B_z-C_y\bigr)(AH-DE)=0,
\end{aligned}}
$$

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(E_y-F_x\bigr)(CH-DG)+\bigl(G_t-H_z\bigr)(AF-BE)\\
&-\bigl(E_z-G_x\bigr)(BH-DF)-\bigl(F_t-H_y\bigr)(AG-CE)\\
&+\bigl(E_t-H_x\bigr)(BG-CF)+\bigl(F_z-G_y\bigr)(AH-DE)=0.
\end{aligned}}
$$

### 5. Verification of the structure

* **Consistency check (integrable case).** Take $\omega_1=dx,\;\omega_2=dy$, i.e. $A=F=1$ and all other coefficients zero. Every curl vanishes, so both left–hand sides are $0$; the system $dx=0,dy=0$ is indeed integrable (integral surfaces $x=\text{const},y=\text{const}$). ✓
* **Non‑trivial integrable case.** Take $\omega_1=dx,\;\omega_2=x\,dy$: $d\omega_1=0$ and $d\omega_2=dx\wedge dy$, so $d\omega_2\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=dx\wedge dy\wedge dx\wedge(x\,dy)=0$. In the formula, $R(a)=0$ (constants) and $R(e)$ has only $E_y-F_x=0-1=-1$ multiplying $CH-DG=0$, while every other factor carries a vanishing $\Omega$‑coefficient; hence $R(e)=0$. ✓
* **Symmetry.** The second condition is obtained from the first by the simultaneous replacement $A\to E,\;B\to F,\;C\to G,\;D\to H$ *in the curl factors only*; the bilinear $\Omega$‑factors $(CH-DG),(AF-BE),\dots$ are common to both, exactly as expected since both conditions test closure of the *same* ideal generated by $\omega_1,\omega_2$.

### 6. Equivalent compact form

Using the Levi‑Civita symbol $\varepsilon_{ijmn}$ (indices in $\{x,y,z,t\}$), both conditions unify into the single statement
$$\varepsilon_{ijmn}\,a_m\,e_n\,\partial_i p_j=0,\qquad p\in\{a,e\},$$
i.e. $\langle d\omega_p,\,\*(\omega_1\wedge\omega_2)\rangle=0$ for $p=1,2$. This is precisely $d\omega_p\wedge\omega_1\wedge\omega_2=0$, confirming the two boxed scalar equations above are the explicit Frobenius integrability conditions for the given system.
